subtitle: When the Guns of Assaye Turned the Deccan

panels.shot: split composition, half showing Arthur Wellesley on horseback under cannon smoke, half showing Daulat Rao Scindia watching from a distant ridge
panels.action: Arthur Wellesley and Daulat Rao Scindia are juxtaposed in one sweeping frame, Wellesley in stained red coat urging sepoys forward through drifting cannon smoke, Scindia robed and jewelled atop a distant rise above a vast Maratha camp dotted with guns.

dialogue.text: Assaye, 1803: outnumbered red-coated lines cross a river into a storm of Maratha guns, and both Arthur Wellesley and Daulat Rao Scindia gamble the Deccan on one burning afternoon.

i18n.hi: असाये, 1803: कमसंख्या वाले लाल कोट नदी पार कर मराठी तोपों के तूफ़ान में घुसते हैं, और आर्थर वेलज़्ली व दौलत राव शिंदे दोनों दक्खन एक दहकती दोपहर पर दांव पर लगा देते हैं।

panels.shot: wide aerial view of the Deccan plateau
panels.action: A sweeping aerial view of the dry Deccan plateau shows brown fields, winding rivers, scattered villages and distant forts, with faint dust plumes of marching armies on the horizon.

dialogue.text: In the early 1800s the Deccan is no quiet plateau; it is a chessboard of armies, treasuries and treaties, where Maratha sardars and the English Company wrestle for revenue and rule.

i18n.hi: 1800 के शुरुआती सालों में दक्खन शांत पठार नहीं, सेनाओं, खज़ानों और संधियों का शतरंज है, जहाँ मराठी सरदार और इंग्लिश कंपनी राजस्व और राज के लिए भिड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a map spread on a wooden table
panels.action: A close view of a parchment map of central India is spread on a rough wooden table, lines inked for rivers and roads, small wooden blocks marking Poona, Hyderabad, and the domains of Scindia and the Bhonsles.

dialogue.text: The Peshwa’s authority frays, Nizam and Company sign subsidiary alliances, and Daulat Rao Scindia and Raghuji Bhonsle of Nagpur hold great armies but uneasy positions between friend and foe.

i18n.hi: पेशवा की सत्ता उधड़ रही है, निज़ाम और कंपनी सहायक संधियाँ करते हैं, और दौलत राव शिंदे व नागपुर के रघुजी भोसले के पास बड़ी सेनाएँ हैं पर दोस्त-दुश्मन के बीच डगमगाती हालत।

panels.shot: medium split shot, archival style vignettes of both men
panels.action: On one side, Arthur Wellesley stands in neat uniform beside European and Indian officers, finger resting on a map; on the other, Daulat Rao Scindia sits in courtly ease on a cushioned gaddi, courtiers around him and a war standard behind.

dialogue.text: Arthur Wellesley, rising Company commander in India, drives columns through the south to uphold their new treaty with the Peshwa; Scindia, Maratha chief of Gwalior, weighs war and negotiation from his mobile camp.

i18n.hi: आर्थर वेलज़्ली, भारत में उभरता कंपनी कमांडर, दक्षिण में स्तंभों को दौड़ाता है ताकि नई पेशवा संधि निभाए; ग्वालियर के मराठी सरदार शिंदे चलते-फिरते डेरों से जंग या बातचीत तौलते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Maratha encampment with artillery lines
panels.action: A broad view of a Maratha camp near Assaye shows rows of heavy guns on wooden carriages, oxen teams, European-style drilled infantry lines in white cotton and coloured turbans, and cavalry forming beyond.

dialogue.text: Near the village of Assaye, Scindia and Bhonsle forces mass with perhaps five times Wellesley’s number, their artillery park thick, their infantry drilled in European fashion, their cavalry still the old Maratha strength.

i18n.hi: असाये गाँव के पास शिंदे और भोसले की सेनाएँ शायद वेलज़्ली से पाँच गुना जुटती हैं, तोपखाना घना, पैदल फौज यूरोपीय ढंग से सिखी, घुड़सवार अभी भी वही पुरानी मराठी ताकत।

panels.shot: distant long shot from behind Scindia, looking at the plain and rivers
panels.action: From behind Daulat Rao Scindia’s shoulder, the viewer sees the plain below: the winding Kailna and Juah rivers encircling Assaye, lines of Maratha guns sited along the bank, and British columns a distant line of dust.

dialogue.text: Assaye lies between two channels, the Kailna and the Juah, a loop of water and mud. Here Scindia’s generals and their allies anchor their guns, believing the rivers will break any English advance.

i18n.hi: असाये दो धाराओं, कएलना और जुआह के बीच है, पानी और कीचड़ की मेढ़; यहीं शिंदे के सरदार और साथी अपनी तोपें गाड़ते हैं, मानते हैं ये नदियाँ किसी भी अंग्रेज़ चढ़ाई को तोड़ देंगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Wellesley astride his horse with officers, pointing toward the river
panels.action: Arthur Wellesley, dust-streaked but composed, sits astride a grey horse with officers around him, gesturing with his sword toward the glinting Kailna where enemy guns can be seen beyond.

dialogue.text: On 23 September 1803 Wellesley finds the Maratha army drawn up in strength across the Kailna. His own forces are weary from marching, his numbers far fewer, yet he chooses not to wait.

i18n.hi: 23 सितंबर 1803 को वेलज़्ली देखता है कि मराठी सेना कएलना के उस पार मजबूती से पंक्तिबद्ध है; उसकी खुद की फौज थकी, संख्या कम, फिर भी वह ठहरने का फैसला नहीं करता।

panels.shot: tight medium on Wellesley and a senior officer in urgent consultation
panels.action: Wellesley leans forward in his saddle, face intent, speaking to a senior officer who gestures anxiously toward the distant guns and the sun already slanting downward.

dialogue.text: If we give them the night, they will slip away or be stronger by morning.

i18n.hi: अगर रात दे दी, तो वे या तो खिसक जाएँगे, या सुबह तक और मज़बूत हो जाएँगे।

panels.shot: wide shot showing British-Company line forming opposite the river
panels.action: Lines of British and sepoy infantry form along the near bank of the Kailna, colours fluttering lightly, while ahead the river glints shallow but wide; smoke hangs over the far bank where Maratha guns wait, their crews poised.

dialogue.text: His dispatch will later admit he was heavily outnumbered, yet he orders a bold flank: cross the Kailna, threaten the enemy’s left, and close before their artillery can rearrange.

i18n.hi: बाद की रिपोर्ट में मानता है कि भारी संख्या में पीछे था, फिर भी वह हिम्मती बाजू बनाता है: कएलना पार करो, दुश्मन का बायाँ मोर्चा धमकाओ, और तोपें नई कतार बाँधें उससे पहले पास जा भिड़ो।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from water level as troops wade across under fire
panels.action: From the surface of the Kailna, sepoys and British soldiers are frozen mid-stride in waist-deep water, muskets held high; behind them standards tilt, while splashes erupt nearby as enemy cannonballs crash into the river.

dialogue.text: As they step into the Kailna the Maratha gunners open. Round after round shrieks over the water. Blakiston remembers the river as a gauntlet, the ford littered with men and broken gear.

i18n.hi: जैसे ही कएलना में उतरते हैं, मराठी तोपची दाग खोल देते हैं; गोले पर गोले पानी के ऊपर चीखते हैं, ब्लैकिस्टन को यह नदी एक मौत की गलियारा लगती है, घाट टूटे आदमियों और बिखरे सामान से पटी।

panels.shot: dynamic medium shot of Wellesley in mid-crossing, horse rearing as a shot strikes nearby
panels.action: Wellesley’s horse rears in the shallows, eyes wild, as a cannon shot lands close, sending up spray; Wellesley leans low, jaw set, steadying the animal while officers and orderlies press around him.

dialogue.text: Wellesley rides in the thick of it. In his own account, more than one horse is shot under him that afternoon, and his staff fall beside him as the guns search for their targets.

i18n.hi: वेलज़्ली खुद बीच घमासान में घोड़ा दौड़ाता है; अपनी लिखाई में मानेगा कि उस दोपहर उसके नीचे से एक से ज़्यादा घोड़े गिराए गए, और स्टाफ उसके पास ही गिरते रहे, जब तोपें उसे निशाना बनाकर थूकती रहीं।

panels.shot: long shot from Maratha gun-line perspective as the British reform on the far bank
panels.action: From behind a Maratha cannon, the viewer sees British and sepoy units scrambling up the muddy far bank, colours lifting, officers shouting, as gunners ram charges and infantry in Maratha ranks ready their muskets.

dialogue.text: Against expectation, the crossing holds. Wellesley’s line reforms under fire on the far bank, its flank nearer the Maratha left, forcing their artillery to twist and their formations to pivot in haste.

i18n.hi: उम्मीद के उलट, पार उतरना जम जाता है; वेलज़्ली की पंक्ति दूसरी तरफ़ गोलियों के बीच फिर से सीधी होती है, अब बाजू मराठी बाएँ पंख के और पास, जिससे उनकी तोपें मुड़नी पड़ती हैं और कतारें हड़बड़ाहट में घूमती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Maratha artillery line in action, smoke and disciplined crews
panels.action: A long line of Maratha guns spits smoke across the plain, crews of gunners in turbans and sashes moving in drilled rhythm with ramrods and matchcords as their officers point toward the advancing enemy.

dialogue.text: Cooper’s study underlines this moment: the Maratha artillery is no mere ornament. Its crews, some shaped by European drill, fire rapidly and with effect, breaking gaps in the advancing red and khaki ranks.

i18n.hi: कूपर की पढ़ाई इसी पल को रेखांकित करती है: मराठी तोपखाना सिर्फ़ दिखावा नहीं, कुछ यूरोपीय ड्रिल झेल चुके दल तेज़ और असरदार आग बरसाते हैं, बढ़ती लाल-खाकी कतारों में चौड़े छेद कर देते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Wellesley ordering a charge, his face strained
panels.action: Wellesley, face lined with strain and sweat, raises his sword and signals forward, while behind him British infantry fix bayonets and sepoys grip their muskets, preparing to surge toward the gun line.

dialogue.text: There is no standing here. We must have those guns.

i18n.hi: यहाँ टिकने का सवाल नहीं, हर हाल में वे तोपें हमें चाहिए।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of British and sepoy infantry advancing in line toward the guns
panels.action: A low-angle view shows British and sepoy infantry in extended line advancing step by step over the open field toward the looming silhouettes of Maratha guns, smoke swirling around them, some files visibly thinned.

dialogue.text: They close the distance under shot and shell. Wellesley later notes the casualties with grim precision: about 1,568 killed and wounded from his side in a few hours’ work.

i18n.hi: वे गोलों और बमों की बारिश में फासला घटाते हैं; वेलज़्ली बाद में ठंडी गिनती से लिखता है – बस कुछ घंटों में उसके पक्ष से लगभग 1,568 मरे या जख़्मी पड़े।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Maratha officer looking back anxiously toward Scindia’s distant position
panels.action: A Maratha officer at the gun line, sabre in hand, looks back over his shoulder toward a distant ridge where riders cluster around a figure seated under a canopy, suggesting Scindia’s vantage point.

dialogue.text: Maratha command is not a single hand. Scindia himself keeps to the rear, his generals managing this front, their eyes on the field and on the power balance beyond one day’s fight.

i18n.hi: मराठी कमान एक हाथ में नहीं, खुद शिंदे पीछे रहते हैं, यह मोर्चा उनके सरदार सँभालते हैं, नज़र एक साथ मैदान पर और उस ताक़त के तराजू पर जो सिर्फ़ एक दिन की लड़ाई से आगे जाता है।

panels.shot: chaotic wide shot of hand-to-hand struggle around the guns, but bloodless
panels.action: Around a row of cannons, British, sepoy and Maratha soldiers press in close; bodies jostle, muskets raised, bayonets thrust, swords swung, and gunners abandon or defend their pieces amid dust and smoke, no wounds shown.

dialogue.text: The fight at the batteries is brutal but quick. In the swirl of smoke, men wrestle control of the guns that have hammered them since the river. Soon their muzzles point in a new direction.

i18n.hi: बैटरी के पास की जंग नंगी और तेज़ है; धुएँ के भँवर में आदमी उन तोपों के लिए भिड़ते हैं जो नदी से ही उन्हें कूटती आई थीं, और जल्द ही उनकी नालें दूसरी दिशा में घूम जाती हैं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of the battlefield as Maratha lines begin to break away
panels.action: From above, the battlefield spreads below: the captured gun line now aligned with Wellesley’s troops, while beyond, pockets of Maratha infantry and cavalry begin to peel away, streams of riders heading off the field.

dialogue.text: Once the guns are lost, the balance shifts. Portions of the Maratha line hold and fall back in order, others melt away. The field is not annihilation, but it is a clear tactical defeat.

i18n.hi: तोपें हाथ से गईं, तो तराज़ू झुक जाता है; मराठी पंक्ति के कुछ हिस्से मोर्चा सँभालते पीछे हटते हैं, कुछ गल जाते हैं, मैदान पूरा सफ़ाया नहीं, पर हार साफ़-साफ़ रणकौशल की है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Wellesley in the smoky aftermath, dismounted, hat in hand
panels.action: In the smoky, dust-heavy evening light, Wellesley stands dismounted amid scattered equipment and weary soldiers, hat in hand, face sombre as he listens to an officer reading casualty figures from a crumpled paper.

dialogue.text: In his dispatches of 24 and 25 September, Wellesley does not write like an easy victor. He lists the losses, notes his officers killed and wounded, and acknowledges how narrow the passage had been.

i18n.hi: 24–25 सितंबर की अपनी चिट्ठियों में वेलज़्ली आसान फ़तह जैसा नहीं लिखता, नुक़सान गिनता है, मरे और जख़्मी अफ़सरों के नाम दर्ज करता है, और मानता है कि राह कितनी तंग रही।

panels.shot: wide shot of captured guns lined up, silhouettes against the dusk
panels.action: Rows of captured cannons stand in a long line on the field as dusk falls, their iron barrels dark silhouettes against a fading sky, British and sepoy guards resting nearby.

dialogue.text: Around ninety-eight Maratha guns, by British count, change hands. Cooper will later argue that this loss of artillery and trained cadres weakens Scindia-Bhonsle military power across the Deccan far beyond one day’s numbers.

i18n.hi: करीब अट्ठानवे मराठी तोपें, अंग्रेज़ हिसाब से, हाथ बदलती हैं; कूपर आगे लिखेगा कि इस तोपखाने और सिखाए दलों की हानि ने शिंदे–भोसले की सैन्य शक्ति को पूरे दक्खन में एक दिन की गिनती से कहीं ज़्यादा खोखला किया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Scindia in a lamplit tent, listening to a messenger
panels.action: Daulat Rao Scindia sits in a lamplit tent, shadowed, as a dust-covered messenger bows and reports, hands spread in a gesture of loss; behind them a small table bears a folded campaign map.

dialogue.text: Maratha accounts from that exact evening are sparse; later Peshwa records speak instead of treaties and losses. But across the next months Scindia and Bhonsle make terms that concede territory and revenue to the Company.

i18n.hi: उसी शाम के मराठी बयान कम हैं, बाद की पेशवाई काग़ज़ी कहानी ज़्यादा संधियों और नुकसानों की बात करती है; पर अगले महीनों में शिंदे और भोसले ऐसी शर्तें मानते हैं जो कंपनी को ज़मीन और आमदनी सौंपती हैं।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Wellesley writing by candlelight
panels.action: Wellesley sits at a small campaign desk under a canvas awning, writing by candlelight, his uniform loosened, quill moving steadily as outside, silhouettes of sentries and distant campfires glow in the dark.

dialogue.text: I have gained a victory, but at such an expense as to give me reason to doubt whether I should do the same again.

i18n.hi: मैंने जीत तो पा ली, पर इतनी कीमत पर कि सोचता हूँ, शायद दोबारा ऐसी राह चुनना न चाहूँ।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot blending Assaye field with later maps of British dominance
panels.action: A visual blend shows the empty, quiet field of Assaye with abandoned gun carriages, overlaid ghost-like with later maps of British-controlled India, the Company’s territories spreading across the subcontinent.

dialogue.text: Assaye does not end the Marathas; later campaigns and politics will reshape that story. But it marks the Deccan turning, the Company’s power rooted now not just in treaties, but in captured guns and seasoned officers.

i18n.hi: असाये मराठों का अंत नहीं, आगे की मुहिमें और सियासत कहानी बदलती रहेंगी; पर यह दक्खन की करवट है, जहाँ कंपनी की पकड़ अब सिर्फ़ काग़ज़ी संधियों से नहीं, पकड़ी गई तोपों और पके अफ़सरों से भी जड़ पकड़ती है।

panels.shot: dual close-up fading between Wellesley’s lined face and a stylised profile of Scindia
panels.action: A close-up of Wellesley’s weathered face fades into the stylised profile of Daulat Rao Scindia, both gazes cast outward, with a faint echo of the Assaye field between them.

dialogue.text: Today, the field of Assaye reminds us that empires can turn on a single hard choice, that victory may bleed the victors as much as the defeated, and that behind every captured gun stands a long, unfinished struggle for power.

i18n.hi: आज का असाये का मैदान याद दिलाता है कि साम्राज्य कभी-कभी एक ही सख़्त फैसले पर मुड़ जाते हैं, जीत विजेताओं को भी उतना ही लहूलुहान कर सकती है जितना हारे हुए को, और हर कब्ज़ाई गई तोप के पीछे ताक़त की एक लंबी, अधूरी जंग खड़ी रहती है।

title_i18n.hi: असाये ने मराठी तोपों को लहुलुहान किया

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Guns of Assaye Turned the Deccan
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब असाये की तोपों ने दक्खन की बाज़ी पलटी
